title: RTP or VN maker graphics for card games.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
For those who didn't see this yet, even though I've talked a lot about it in the past, I made a card game.
I am remaking the system, to break the limits of using the RPG maker database since I use enemies in the database to store the data for cards. I would love to tell you more about those limits and how and why to break out, but that is not going to be the topic of this thread.
I do remake this with the javascript knowledge I've learned since I made the original game. And I try to do this in a way, that I can easily create several games with the same sytem, yet become very different card games.
To take this to the test, I am creating 2 different sets of cards:
- A fantasy battle card game, using RTP of VX Ace, MV and MZ
- A roleplaying card game, using VN Maker default graphics
And even though I use the graphics everyone has seen before, I kind of love how they turn out.
The first card shows the VN Maker version, and the second card is made with RTP.
(Skill Icon in the upper right corner is a VX Ace remake by Avery.)
You might notice the card in the VN version is much less detailed than the RTP one. And that is true. With my system, I show most card info in-game, instead of printed on the card. This is true for both games. But since the VN cards are not a battle game, I do not have use for things like health and attack. Instead there are other ways to show card details.
To make maximum use if the limited character set I have, I need to re-use them in different ways. I have 3 outfits for most characters and a bunch of different moods. And I have a ton of locations which all come in morning, daytime and night setting.
So to make different cards, I just make multiple combinations, like:
Ace, neutral, in PJ's, during the day, in his bedroom
Ace, neutral, in uniform, during the day, in the classroom
Ace, happy, in personal clothing, at night, at the fair
Daniel, neutral, in PJ's, during the day, in his bedroom
Daniel, neutral, in uniform, during the day, in the classroom
Daniel, happy, in personal clothing, at night, at the fair
And so on, and so on. This would look like this:
So now I have 6 cards, all different, while they all have at least 2 things in common with at least 2 different cards.
If the location, the outfit, the mood, and the time of day are all important stats in the game, then those cards might be more detailed than the cards I made with RTP.
I could make locations a thing in the RTP set as well, but that wouldn't make much sense. What is a water spirit doing in the lava cave or a fire spirit at sea. See, with RTP I have to be more careful about which character goes where.
I think it is needles to say that creating cards is a time consuming aspect. And I need at least 200 different cards in a single set to make anything playable...
To be clear... I plan to make 2 games so in the end I will create both sets. But which set one should I go for first?
Spoiler:
Other themes I've worked on.
I have made a game with the Pop!Horror City and Pop!Forrest Slasher sets by Vexed Enigma before.
I've planned to recreate this game with different themes before, but never made it all the way trough.
Another theme I tries before is the Medieval collection by PVG Games.
Cards would look more like this:
Those sets provides me with an unlimited supply of characters. I payed quite a penny for the set and I definitely plan to use it for a future game, but maybe not in the card games...
The problem is: All cards have the exact same pose. No matter if they are a housewife the captain of the guard. This is needed for all the parts to be compatible, but it does make the cards very repetitive.
